abstract: We construct a rational two-parameter family of Diophantine sextuples with exactly one regular quadruple and two regular quintuples on a nonempty open subset. The construction starts from a Möbius relation between two entries that makes the classical regular fifths of a quadruple mutually compatible. An explicit factorization distinguishes this relation from the Piezas product condition. We rationalize three of the four source square conditions while moving actual entries, then specialize a quadratic discriminant so the fourth condition becomes a rational square. Two conic parametrizations give all six entries and all fifteen signed rational roots. A nonzero exact entry-Jacobian minor proves that the image has dimension two. Exact regularity and division-polynomial tests distinguish the family from direct outputs of the cited order-three and two-regular-quadruple constructions; we do not assert independence from every birational correspondence. An elliptic subfamily has a strong member; an explicit fractional-linear transformation gives infinitely many sextuples with no regular quadruple and exactly two regular quintuples. A nontorsion proof and Kummer-class calculation supply infinitely many rational lifts. Standalone rational-arithmetic verifiers and independent universal symbolic audits accompany the proof. The nonzero regular fifth of the distinguished regular quadruple gives four further compatible edges, leaving two separately retained rational-square conditions for a seventh entry. No simultaneous rational solution of those conditions is supplied, and no nonexistence claim is made. The contribution is a rationally parametrized source inside the established regular-closure framework, with complete root data for continued septuple research.

title: A rational two-parameter Diophantine sextuple construction by discriminant cancellation
